messages.content: what is a place you like to visit?
i do not visit places myself, but i can talk about places you enjoy. is there a place you often go when you want a quiet moment?
i like the library. i know the room, and there is a chair near the window where i usually read.
that sounds like a place you know well. what do you enjoy most about that chair and window?
i can see a tree outside. i do not always read much. sometimes i just sit there.
then the library gives you more than books. it is also a place where you can sit quietly and look outside.
my brother says i should only go if i plan to read a whole book.
you can enjoy a library without finishing a whole book on each visit. if you are not sure what is okay there, you can ask someone who works in that library.
say that in a shorter way.
you can enjoy sitting quietly with a book without finishing it that day. if you are not sure what is okay in that library, you can ask someone who works there.
just say something kind about my quiet time.
it sounds good to have a place where you can slow down for a while.
my grandfather said something kind to me today, and i want to remember it. i do not remember every word.
you can write down the part you remember clearly and keep the rest as your own explanation of how it felt. that keeps his known words apart from anything you might add.
use only simple words. he said he was happy i came to visit. i remember that part.
then you could write: my grandfather told me he was happy i came to visit.
i think he also said something about the garden, but i am not sure what.
you can leave that part out or say you do not remember it clearly. you do not have to remember everything to keep the important part.
i want one short note that keeps the part i know.
my grandfather told me he was happy i came to visit today. i want to remember that.
should i add that he said i was his best friend?
not unless he said that and you remember it. the fact that the visit felt good does not give us those words.
why is the small note enough?
it keeps something real that was important to you without adding a larger story you do not know.
my friend wants to write, and i want to draw. can we spend time together without doing the same thing?
yes. you can share a place and some time while working on different things. what kind of room would work for both of you?
the kitchen table has room, but i like to talk while drawing and she needs quiet to write.
then talk about the quiet before you start. you could work quietly for a while and talk when you both take a break, if that works for both of you.
give me a shorter plan.
you could work quietly for a while, then put the work down and talk together.
i do not want her to think i am sad if i am not talking.
you can say that you enjoy being with her even when you are both quiet. quiet does not have to mean something is wrong.
write one short message for her.
i would like to draw while you write. we can keep the room quiet, and then talk when we take a break.
what should we choose before starting?
you could choose when to take the break and whether that time of quiet works for both of you.
write about a child choosing one part of a good day to tell at school.

a girl had a good day with her family. in the morning, she helped her father make breakfast. later, she walked with her sister and found a small flower by the road. in the afternoon, her grandmother showed her a photo of the house where she once lived. when the teacher asked for a short story about the day, the girl first wanted to tell every detail. then she chose the part about the photo. it had made her ask a question she had never thought of before: what had the garden looked like when her grandmother was little? she wrote that question at the end of her story.
did choosing the photo mean breakfast was not good?
no. she chose one part for a short story. the other parts of the day could still have been good.
give me the answer another way.
no. breakfast could still have been good. she only needed one part for the short story.
why did she choose the photo?
it made her think of a new question about the garden when her grandmother was little.
make that answer shorter.
the photo made her think of a new question about the old garden.
what did she write at the end?
she wrote her question about the garden.
give me a little story and ask one question i can answer from it.

a man left a letter on the table before going to work. his daughter found it after breakfast. the letter asked her to call her grandmother in the afternoon. she put it by her book so she would remember. where did the daughter put the letter?
by her book.
yes. she put it by her book so she would remember the call.
ask me who wrote the letter.
who wrote the letter?
her grandmother?
the story does not say who wrote it. it says the man left it on the table. leaving a letter and writing it are not always the same thing.
was your question a good one if i needed to know the answer from the story?
not for that goal. the story did not say who wrote the letter, so i should ask about a detail it does give.
ask a better question.
when was the daughter asked to call her grandmother?
in the afternoon.
yes. the letter asked her to call in the afternoon.
my friend says she wants me to sit with her while she cleans her room. should i start moving things for her?
you could ask first. she may want help with the cleaning, or she may only want you to be with her while she does it herself.
ask the question using simple words.
would you like me to help clean, or just sit and talk with you while you do it?
she says just sit, but i feel as if i should be helping more.
you are still doing what she asked: being with her while she works. you do not have to change her request into a different kind of help.
say that in a shorter way.
you can sit with her because that is what she asked for. being there can be the help she wants.
what if i see a book on the floor and want to put it away?
you can ask where she wants it before moving it. that keeps her choice about her room clear.
write a short thing i could say.
do you want me to leave this book here, or put it away for you?
write a story about a child looking at himself in a mirror before a family visit.

a boy was getting ready for a visit to his aunt. he stood by the mirror and looked at himself. he saw some food by his mouth. he went to wash his face, then came back and looked again. his face was clean now. he took his book and went to meet his father by the door. they left together for the visit.
tell that story in fewer words.

a boy looked at himself in a mirror before a visit. he saw food by his mouth and went to wash his face. when he came back, his face was clean. he took his book and met his father by the door before they left.
were there two children because the boy saw himself?
no. there was one boy looking at himself in a mirror.
where did he go after taking his book?
to meet his father by the door.
why did he wash his face?
he saw food by his mouth.
what changed when he looked again?
his face was clean.
write a short message from me to my cousin. i want to say i found her book and will bring it tomorrow.
i found your book and will bring it tomorrow.
now write it as if my cousin is telling her mother about my message.
my cousin found my book and will bring it tomorrow.
why is your book now my book?
because the person talking changed. in your message, you are talking to your cousin about her book. when she talks to her mother, she calls that same book my book.
did the person who found it change?
no. you are still the person who found it. your cousin is only telling someone else what happened.
what if she says i found my book?
then she would be saying she found it herself, which is different from your original message.
write it as if she is talking to her mother again.
my cousin found my book and will bring it tomorrow.
now go back to my first message and add please let me know if you need it before then.
i found your book and will bring it tomorrow. please let me know if you need it before then.
there are two books on the table and three books on the shelf. i move one from the table to the shelf. do i now have six books?
no. moving one book does not add a new book. you still have five books: one on the table and four on the shelf.
what if my sister brings another book into the room?
then you have one more book than before. if it is with those five, there are six books in the room.
bring is not the same as give, right?
right. bringing the book into the room does not by itself tell us she gives it to you to keep.
so how many of the six are mine?
you have not said which of the first five are yours to keep or whether your sister gives you the new one. knowing the number of books is not enough to answer whose they are.
say that in a more simple way.
you have not said which books are yours to keep. knowing there are six books in the room does not tell us that all six are yours.
what question should i ask if i only want the number on the shelf after the first move?
how many books are on the shelf now?
and the answer before my sister comes in?
four books.
my friend told me her sister is coming home tomorrow after a long time away. i want a warm reply, but i do not know her sister well.
you can be happy for your friend without saying you know her sister well. you could say: that sounds good. i hope you have a happy visit together.
give me just the message.
that sounds good. i hope you have a happy visit together.
can i say i have wanted to see her for so long?
only if that is true for you. from what you said, you do not know her well, so that might not be the meaning you want.
i want to say i can see my friend is happy.
you could say: you sound happy that she is coming home. i hope you enjoy your time together.
is sound happy different from saying i know every feeling she has?
yes. sound happy is about how her message seems to you. it does not say you know every feeling she has.
say that more simply.
you can say her message sounds happy without saying you know every feeling she has.
just give the message again.
you sound happy that she is coming home. i hope you enjoy your time together.
i finished my book last night, but i keep thinking about the last page today.
finishing the reading does not always end the thinking. was there a question on that page that stayed with you?
there was a choice a person made. i am not sure i would have made the same choice.
that can give you a useful way to talk about the story. what information did the person have when making the choice, and what would you have wanted to know?
the person chose to leave home, but we did not know whether she would come back.
then one question is what she wanted from leaving, and another is whether she wanted to return. the story may leave some of that open.
ask a simple question i can think about.
what did she want when she chose to leave home?
i think she wanted to see another place without saying she would never come home.
then she might want to leave for now without choosing to stay away for the rest of her life. that could be one way to read it, if the story gives you reasons for it.
make the answer shorter.
she may want to leave now without giving up the idea of coming home later.
do you know for sure that is the right reading?
no. i only have the details you gave. your idea is one possible way to understand them.
what is the difference between how many chairs are in the room and where are the chairs?
the first asks for a number. the other asks for a place or places.
there are three chairs: one by the window and two by the table. answer the first question.
there are three chairs in the room.
now answer where they are without using the number three again.
one chair is by the window, and two are by the table.
ask me a question that could make me answer blue.
what color is the chair by the window?
blue. does that answer how many chairs there are?
no. blue is a color, not the number of chairs.
now ask me a question that could make me answer in the kitchen.
which room are the chairs in?
in the kitchen. put everything together in a few short sentences.
there are three chairs in the kitchen. the blue chair is by the window, and two other chairs are by the table.
what do you not know about the other two chairs?
you have not told me their color.
write a story about two friends sitting quietly before talking.

two friends met by a window after a busy day. one had brought a book, and the other had brought a drawing she wanted to show. they sat quietly for a while, looking at the garden. neither felt a need to begin with a large explanation. after some time, the friend with the drawing put it on the table. she asked what the other thought of it, and they began to talk about the color of the house in the picture. the quiet had given them a calm start to their visit.
tell me only what happened after the quiet part.
after some time, the friend with the drawing put it on the table. they began to talk about the color of the house in it. the quiet had given them a calm start to their visit.
does sitting quietly mean either friend had to be sad?
no. the story does not say they were sad. being quiet can have more than one meaning.
ask me a question about something the story gives.
what did one friend bring to show the other?
a drawing. now ask about where they sat.
where did the friends sit?
by a window.
yes. they sat by a window and looked at the garden before talking.
i want help choosing a book, but i do not want you to choose everything for me.
i can ask questions about the choices and what you want. what kind of reading would you like today?
i want something short and calm.
then we can use short and calm as things to look for. what are the books you are choosing between?
one has a quiet story about a family. the other has a long journey with many changes. the first is shorter.
from what you said, the family story sounds more like what you want today. you can still choose for yourself.
give me a shorter answer.
the family story sounds more like what you want today. you can still choose for yourself.
what if i begin to want the journey book more after all?
then that new wish is useful information too. the goal was to help you choose a book you want. you can still change what you want.
say it more simply.
you can change what you want as you think. i can help, but you are still the person choosing the book.
just give me one question to ask myself.
which book do i most want to begin today?
what does i only moved the book mean?
it could mean you moved the book but did nothing else to it. it could also mean the book was the one object you moved. more information can make the meaning clear.
give the two possible ideas in a more simple way.
it could mean you moved the book but did not do anything else. it could also mean the book was the only object you moved. more words could make it clear.
i mean i moved the book, but i did not read it.
then you could say: i moved the book, but i did not read it.
what would i say if i moved the book and left the other objects where they were?
you could say: the book was the only object i moved.
can changing the place of only change what someone thinks the sentence is about?
yes. only can go with different parts of a sentence. when more than one meaning is possible, you can use more words to make your own meaning clear.
give me a basic rule for writing a sentence with only.
when only could mean more than one thing, add enough words to make the meaning you want clear.
what information did i give that made my first sentence more clear?
you said you moved the book but did not read it.
my friend asked if i could help move a table today. i am not free until tomorrow. i do not want her to think i do not care.
you can say what you can do rather than making up a reason. tell her you cannot help today and that tomorrow is possible, if that would still help.
write a short message.
i cannot help with the table today, but i am free tomorrow. would that still be useful?
she says it has to move today. should i keep saying tomorrow until she says yes?
no. she has told you tomorrow does not work for this need. you can be sorry you cannot help today without saying your free time tomorrow is a solution to her problem.
make that explanation more simple.
she needs help today, and you are free tomorrow. those do not work together for this task. you can say you are sorry you cannot help today.
would saying no mean we cannot be friends?
no. not being free for one request does not mean you cannot be friends.
give me that answer another way.
no. you can still care about your friend even when you cannot help with this one task.
end with one kind sentence i can send.
i am sorry i cannot help today. i hope you find someone who can.
write a story where a small note is useful in both the morning and evening.

a woman wrote a note before leaving home in the morning. it said to bring the old photo when she went to see her sister. she put it by the door, where she would look before leaving. when evening came, she was tired and thinking about dinner. she saw the note and remembered the photo. she took it from the shelf and put it in her book. at the visit, her sister was happy to see it. they talked about the day in the photo, and the woman was happy she had left herself a note.
give me just the last sentence.
the woman was happy she had left herself a note.
why was the note useful in the evening if she wrote it in the morning?
she could read it later, when she needed to remember the photo. writing it in the morning helped her remember it in the evening.
say it another way.
she wrote the note before leaving in the morning and read it again before the evening visit. it helped her remember to bring the photo.
what did she put the photo in?
her book.
what did her sister do when she saw it?
she was happy to see it, and they talked about the day in the picture.
make this sentence shorter: we might go to the park tomorrow if the weather is good, but we have not chosen yet.
we may go to the park tomorrow if the weather is good.
can i leave out may and say we go to the park tomorrow?
that would sound more sure than the first sentence. you said it was a possible plan, not a choice you had already made.
give me a more simple explanation.
your first sentence says the plan is still open. leaving out may could make it sound as if you had already chosen to go.
what if the weather is good? does that make the visit sure?
not by itself. you also said you have not chosen yet. good weather is one part of the plan, but it does not tell us you will go.
give me a short answer.
no. the weather can be good while the choice is still open.
write one sentence that keeps both parts.
we may go tomorrow if the weather is good, but we have not chosen yet.
why is chosen useful there?
it keeps clear that you have not yet made the choice.
make this short story more simple: a boy returned to the library because he had left his book there. he was worried it would be gone, but he found it on the same table.
a boy went back to the library for the book he had left there. he was worried, but it was still on the table.
can it just say a boy went to the library and found a book?
that would lose important meaning. it would not say the book was his or why he went back.
keep the reason but leave out the feeling.
a boy went back to the library because he had left his book there. he found it on the same table.
what did you leave out?
the part about him feeling worried.
did he become happy at the end?
he may have been happy, but your story did not say that. i should not add it as a fact when making your story shorter.
what would i need to add if i want that feeling in the story?
you could add: he was happy to find his book.
now give me the short story with that new sentence.
a boy went back to the library because he had left his book there. he found it on the same table and was happy to see it.
if i tell you my room is blue, can you know what is outside the window?
no. the color of your room does not tell me what is outside the window. you would need to give me more information about that.
there is a tree outside. can you know what kind?
not from just tree. that is a general word, and it does not give the details needed to know the specific kind.
what if i ask you to make up a story about it instead?
then i can write an example story, as long as we keep clear that the new details are part of the story and not things i know about your real tree.
write one short sentence with no new facts added to what i told you.
there is a tree outside the window of your blue room.
did i tell you the tree was very old?
no. you only said there was a tree outside. you did not say how old it was.
give me a shorter answer.
no. you did not say how old the tree was.
what is useful to do when you need a detail someone has not given?
ask for that detail rather than make up a new fact.
